title: Seat MiniMELF caps on pads and match cylindrical outline
description: Adjusts the MiniMELF component design to ensure proper seating on pads and matches the cylindrical outline as per specifications, improving the fit and visual representation of the component.
body:
**motivation**
The MiniMELF end contacts look like rounded disks beside the body and barely touch their footprint lands. The supplied cylindrical reference has a continuous dark case, short silver end caps, and a narrow identification band set back from one cap.

**after**
Keep the nominal 3.5 mm complete case length established by this PR. Reduce the excessive edge rounding so the case and 0.4 mm contacts read as a continuous cylinder. Make each cap 0.02 mm larger in radius so it seats into the thin pad extrusion; a geometry test now verifies positive volume overlap with both C68883 SOD-80 lands. Add a pale band on the dark body, moved inward to leave more than 0.2 mm of dark material between the band and its adjacent cap. The complete diameter is 1.54 mm, within the [Vishay SOD-80 outline](https://www.vishay.com/docs/85557/ll4148.pdf). The illustration's printed words are surface artwork and are not part of the solid model.

For C68883 / LL4148-GS08, `sod80_p3.5301mm_pl1.44mm_pw1.62mm` now measures **88.43533% exact volumetric IoU**, up from **81.59045%** at this PR's previous geometry, at physical millimeter scale without reference-mesh fitting. The companion footprint discovery [#115](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-footprinter/pull/115) is merged. This exceeds the new 60% target, which is tracked in the separate matcher [PR #3](https://github.com/tscircuit/jlcpcb-jscad-match/pull/3). The full 600-part benchmark was not rerun for this visual revision.

**validation**
- All 265 model tests pass with an extended runner timeout, including physical pad overlap and updated six-view snapshots.
- Build, TypeScript, and format checks pass.
- The SOD-80 top and underside views and both MiniMELF six-view sheets were inspected.

title: Keep zero-length fixed spans in Pipeline9 regional sections
description: Fixes autorouting failure by retaining zero-length fixed spans during regional section assembly, allowing for proper reconstruction of routes in the Pipeline9 autorouter.
body:
## Problem

The exact 96-component T113 fixture contains two identical consecutive fanout points in `fanout:breakout:pcb_breakout_point_68:source-0`. Pipeline9 converts that `1..2` position span into a zero-length fixed route. During the actual `cmn_60` regional fallback, section construction discarded that slice, joined its `0..1` and `2..3` neighbors, and accepted one replacement spanning `0..3`. The stale zero-length identity survived beside its replacement, so reconstruction failed with:

`Pipeline9 could not reconnect mutated preloaded segment "breakout:pcb_breakout_point_68_fixed_168_1"`

## Change

- Retain zero-length fixed slices while contiguous regional sections are assembled, allowing a replacement spanning that position to absorb their source identities.
- Skip a complete assembled section only when the whole section is zero-length, since it has no copper and cannot form a useful fallback port pair.
- Add a deterministic regression using the exact T113 SRJ, trace index 168, actual `cmn_60` bounds and ports, and the accepted replacement captured from the full-board failure.
- Update the exact integration test and PCB SVG with the completed Pipeline9 output.

The exact solver now completes with `solved=true`, `failed=false`, and 42 routed or mutated traces. The resulting board still has downstream routing violations: strict repository DRC reports 69 errors and `tsci check shorts` reports 47 physical shorts. Those require separate reproductions and root fixes.

## Validation

- Focused canonical ownership, zero-length reconstruction, and exact T113 tests: 3 passed, 28 assertions
- Exact 96-component Pipeline9 run: `solved=true`, `failed=false`, `error=null`, 42 routes
- `bun run build`
- `git diff --check`

title: Repro: Pipeline 9 silently narrows requested trace width
description: Reproduces a bug where Pipeline 9 narrows a requested 0.4 mm trace width to 0.2375 mm instead of finding a legal detour, highlighting a flaw in the autorouting logic.
body:
## Repro

Pipeline 9 is asked to route one 0.4 mm trace. The board is 30 × 20 mm, with two unrelated rectangular obstacles near its center. They leave a 0.50 mm shortcut, but 0.4 mm copper plus 0.13 mm clearance on each side needs 0.66 mm. There is over 7 mm of free board space above and below the obstacles; a compliant route is not blocked by the board outline.

With the board-wide minimum at 0.1 mm, Pipeline 9 reports success and chooses the shortcut at 0.2375 mm. The control keeps the **same board, pads, obstacles, endpoints, clearance, and requested 0.4 mm width**; changing only the board-wide minimum to 0.4 mm makes Pipeline 9 find a legal 0.4 mm route around an obstacle, more than 5 mm from the board edge. Thus the router has a feasible full-width path in this geometry. Both panels are generated from actual solver outputs; the gray rectangle shows the board bounds.

![Actual Pipeline 9 output and full-width control](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Abse2001/tscircuit-autorouter/codex/repro-pipeline9-trace-width/tests/repro/__snapshots__/pipeline9-silent-trace-width-neckdown.snap.svg)

## Where the width is lost

This reproduces the Game Boy power-path problem: Core converts a TSX trace `thickness="0.4mm"` into `source_trace.min_trace_thickness = 0.4`, then puts it in SRJ as `connection.nominalTraceWidth = 0.4` (`getSimpleRouteJsonFromCircuitJson.ts`). SRJ has only a global `minTraceWidth = 0.1` and no per-connection *minimum*. `TraceWidthSolver` tries nominal, a midpoint, then silently falls back to the board minimum when clearance is insufficient. The resulting board can be geometrically DRC-clean while violating the authored current-carrying width.

The fix should preserve the distinction between a preferred width and a hard per-connection minimum across Core/SRJ/Pipeline 9. The router should take the available compliant detour here; if no compliant route exists, it should report a constraint failure rather than silently narrow the wire. This PR is repro-only, with no solver changes. Related existing issue: #1721.

## Validation

- Focused repro: pass.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`: pass.
- `git diff --check`: pass.

body:
Update the pinned `@tscircuit/length-matching-solver` commit from `96cca678` to `9a5cd6cf`, bringing in the retained-lead clearance fix from https://github.com/tscircuit/length-matching-solver/pull/70.

The old pin causes the captured AM3352 DDR_D0 bus matcher to exhaust its search when unchanged leads overlap existing clearance regions. The new commit preserves unchanged lead geometry while checking newly introduced meander copper. This repository directly imports that package in `lib/solvers/length-matching-post-processing-solver.ts` and bundles it into `@tscircuit/capacity-autorouter`; no core or fanout API change is needed.

**Merge dependency:** #70 merged into the reproduction branch; https://github.com/tscircuit/length-matching-solver/pull/69 is still open against main. The pin identifies the exact merged fix commit. Merge that parent PR before landing this consumer update.

Validation:
- Installed the exact Git dependency `9a5cd6cf4658505da600cec432933e091147e83d` into an isolated validation environment.
- Ran this checkout's `LengthMatchingPostProcessingSolver` with the captured post-differential-pair geometry from the upstream `fixtures/am3352-ddr-d0/input.json.gz`, a two-member DDR_D0/DDR_D5 bus and 0.635 mm skew tolerance. Retained all 48 routes and 908 obstacles. No physical differential pairs were passed because this capture is already after that stage.
- **Solved in 24.465 seconds / 72 steps.** Lengths: 25.7331015268 and 25.7331015260 mm; skew about 7.9e-10 mm.
- Asserted exact preservation of endpoints, vias, and unrelated routes.
- `git diff --check` passed. Full autorouter build/suite not run for this dependency-only update; validation exercised the consuming source stage and exact updated dependency.

This confirms the captured matching stage, not full-board connectivity, absolute DDR length limits, or physical signoff. No lockfile is added because `bunfig.toml` explicitly disables lockfile saving.

After this merges and an autorouter release is published, core and tscircuit need dependency bumps to that released version: their current `^0.0.900` ranges exclude later `0.0.x` versions. Refresh consumer lockfiles/bundles and release through the usual chain. Merging this PR alone does not update already-published core/CLI bundles. No speculative consumer version bump is included because a release containing this fix does not exist yet.

title: Resolve canonical roots in Pipeline9 via validation
description: Fixes autorouting failure by resolving route and obstacle identities to canonical nets in Pipeline9 during regional via validation.
body:
## Problem

After the closed-route serialization fix on `main`, Pipeline9 reaches a second ownership mismatch in regional via validation. Generated fixed routes carry canonical `rootConnectionName` values, while board obstacles carry member trace and port IDs. Passing those two forms directly to the generic connectivity API makes the exact T113 route `source_trace_44_fixed_262_13` treat its own `pcb_smtpad_139` as foreign copper.

The full exact run consequently stops at `No path found for source_trace_194` even though the rejected candidate only intersects copper from its own net.

## Change

- Resolve route and obstacle identities to canonical nets at the Pipeline9 regional obstacle-validation boundary.
- Map member IDs before considering an ID as a canonical net key. This preserves the collision case where one string is both a generated net key and a member of another net.
- Keep `circuit-json-to-connectivity-map@0.0.19` and its existing member-ID semantics.
- Add a focused regression that loads the merged, unmodified 96-component T113 fixture and checks the exact same-net pad plus a foreign-net obstacle.
- Update the full exact integration test to prove the solver advances through `source_trace_194` and reaches the next independent reconstruction invariant.

## Visual diff

This PR is stacked on #2592. That PR adds `t113-linux-exact-pipeline9-state.svg` with the exact board and its 342 preloaded traces at the failure boundary. This PR modifies the same file using the same renderer and viewport, adding the 42 routes reached after the canonical ownership fix. The Files changed visual view is therefore a direct before/after of this fix.

## Validation

- Exact canonical-obstacle, NRF ID-collision, and full T113 tests: 3 passed, 30 assertions
- Full exact solver run: 42 routes, then `breakout:pcb_breakout_point_68_fixed_168_1`
- `bun run build`: pass, including declarations
- Fixed SVG rasterized and inspected at 2400 × 1800
- `git diff --check`: pass

Visual reproduction: #2592

Next stacked fix: #2585

title: Reproduce AM3352 DDR_D0 length-matching search exhaustion
description: This PR reproduces a bug where the LengthMatchingSolver exhausts its meander search for DDR_D0, adding a test to confirm the failure without altering production solver functionality.
body:
The AM3352 DDR routing experiment reaches byte-bus matching, then `LengthMatchingSolver` exhausts its meander search for `DDR_D0`. This PR adds the captured standalone input and an opt-in observed-failure test, with no production solver changes.

The failing comparison is `DDR_D0` (`source_net_70`) against `DDR_D5` (`source_net_87`) with 0.635 mm skew tolerance. The test reproduces `LengthMatchingNoSolutionError`, reason `meander-search-exhausted`, and `required 9.9183mm`.

The fixture was captured at the bus matcher constructor after Pipeline 9's differential-pair stage, using capacity-autorouter 0.0.900 and length-matching-solver commit 96cca6783a6e29d12bb1871185efe6ff2257bef8. It preserves all 48 routes and 908 obstacles and removes only later comparison requests that never run before this failure. Gzip keeps the otherwise 5 MB input to about 189 KB; provenance and decompression instructions are included.

This is a reproduction, not a fix or proof that the requested geometry is feasible. The passing test intentionally confirms today's failure and is opt-in to avoid slowing ordinary CI.

```sh
bun install
RUN_AM3352_DDR_REPRO=1 bun test tests/repros/am3352-ddr-d0.test.ts --timeout 9999999
```

Validation:
- Standalone reproduction: **1 pass, 9 assertions, 178.616 seconds, 59 iterations** (Bun 1.3.2 / macOS arm64).
- Default invocation: **1 skipped, 0 failures**.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run build`, and `bun run typecheck:structure`: passed; structural checks report existing warnings.

The original full-pipeline experiment took 876.351 seconds to report the same failure. Board provenance: https://tscircuit.com/seveibar/am3352-dev-board (v1.0.1).


### Final failed `solver.visualize()` snapshot

The test now records the native visualization after the expected failure. The checked-in SVG has a PNG preview below (all layers and plane obstacles overlaid). Snapshot generation reproduced the failure again: 10 assertions passed.

![Final failed solver visualization](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/length-matching-solver/repro/am3352-ddr-d0-length-matching/fixtures/am3352-ddr-d0/final-visualization.png)

Follow-up fix is stacked in #70, which targets this branch and changes the captured regression to require successful matching.

title: Fix DDR length matching blocked by unchanged lead clearances
description: Fixes the issue where the DDR_D0 matcher rejected meanders due to unchanged lead clearances, allowing for successful matching while preserving existing terminal leads.
body:
Stacked on #69; review and merge #69 first. This PR targets its reproduction branch.

The captured DDR_D0 matcher rejected meanders because the replacement includes unchanged straight leads beside existing copper/vias. Those inherited lead clearances caused every candidate on useful segments to fail, even when the new meander copper could fit. The solver eventually raised `LengthMatchingNoSolutionError` requesting another 9.9183 mm.

Preserve the clearance state of a replacement segment only when both endpoints lie within one original same-layer segment (1e-9 mm numerical tolerance), and only when the replacement actually introduces new geometry. Newly introduced segments still undergo bounds, obstacle, via, and foreign-trace checks. Plain straight-segment validation retains its existing behavior. No spacing or length tolerance is relaxed, and no failed solve is converted to success.

The #69 fixture now solves and checks DDR_D0/DDR_D5 skew ≤0.635 mm, exact endpoints/vias, and unchanged unrelated routes. A focused geometry test verifies that new copper is still rejected against obstacles, own-net vias, foreign traces, displaced leads, and different-layer geometry. The native final `solver.visualize()` snapshot and PNG are updated to the successful state.

This change does not repair inherited board DRC violations or establish full-board routing/signoff; it validates the copper added by this matching operation.

Validation:
- Captured DDR regression and snapshot verification: **199 assertions, about 26 seconds / 62 iterations** (previously failed after about 179 seconds).
- Focused retained-lead and blind-via tests: **2 passed**.
- Typecheck, build, structural checks: passed; existing structural warnings remain.

Run the captured regression:

```sh
RUN_AM3352_DDR_REPRO=1 bun test tests/repros/am3352-ddr-d0.test.ts --timeout 9999999
```

![Final successful solver visualization](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/length-matching-solver/fix/am3352-preserve-unchanged-leads/fixtures/am3352-ddr-d0/final-visualization.png)

Full-suite result: **83 passed, 1 opt-in test skipped, 1 timing failure**. `rv1106g2-camera-search.test.ts` exceeded its 45-second limit (54.9 seconds in the fix suite). The same test also fails on the unchanged #69 base when run alone (47.6 seconds). This timing limit was not changed or suppressed; the captured DDR regression was run separately and passes. These wall-clock measurements do not establish a performance improvement for the unrelated camera case.

**Merge update (2026-09-16):** Both feature branches now include the latest main (discovery `728803e`; model library `94e3cda`). The adjacent TSSOP/MiniMELF helper conflict is resolved. Rotated layouts retain pin placement, and unrelated package names remain generic.

This standard footprint makes C68883 evaluable. Together with the independent [MiniMELF outline correction in jscad-electronics #363](https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/pull/363), it passes at **81.59045% volumetric IoU** using exact Manifold comparison without scaling. Discovery alone measures **77.21296%** against the old geometry. With both changes, the full footprint-only benchmark improves **9/600 → 10/600** and evaluated pairs increase **451 → 452**. All 9 earlier passes remain; every other part has identical scores and statuses. Only the eligible C68883 discovery row was regenerated; the other 599 prior derivations are retained unchanged. title: Fix TSSOP/HTSSOP discovery with measured standard footprint candidates
description: Fixes incorrect resolution of TSSOPHTSSOP packages to DFN by generating accurate TSSOP candidates based on metadata, ensuring proper matching and scoring for electronic component footprints.
body:
TSSOP/HTSSOP imports can currently resolve to DFN because the search has a precise DFN seed but relies on optimization for TSSOP. For example, C14347 (TSSOP-24) resolves to `dfn24_…` even with its package hint.

Generate a measured TSSOP candidate when the metadata identifies that standard family. Convert pad-row spacing to TSSOP's inner-gap `w`, account for its fine-pitch spacing adjustment, and preserve pad corners through the existing `rounded` parameter. Exposed pads retain their dimensions and orientation through `thermalpad`. All emitted parameters are supported by the existing Footprinter dependency; there are no new spec tokens, manufacturer selectors, or ranking-score changes.

Hint matching checks complete family tokens and pin counts and stays neutral for conflicting metadata (including TSSOP/SOT descriptions). Existing copper and pin scoring still chooses the winner.

Validation:
- 148 tests pass; typecheck, format check, and ESM/declaration build pass.
- Three JLC-derived pad fixtures with labeled side-by-side SVG snapshots: [C14347](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-footprinter/blob/fix/tssop-package-hints/tests/__snapshots__/jlcpcb-tssop-package-C14347.snap.svg), [C52717](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-footprinter/blob/fix/tssop-package-hints/tests/__snapshots__/jlcpcb-tssop-package-C52717.snap.svg), and [C114177](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-footprinter/blob/fix/tssop-package-hints/tests/__snapshots__/jlcpcb-tssop-package-C114177.snap.svg). Their copper IoUs are 99.93%, 99.95%, and 99.78%. C114177's existing numbered-EP versus `thermalpad` pin-label mismatch remains explicitly asserted.
- Regression coverage includes absent/conflicting/unrelated hints, incorrect pin counts, incompatible topology, and fine-pitch spacing.
- Local check of the 18 TSSOP/HTSSOP parts in our 600-part JLC sample selects TSSOP for 14. With unchanged JSCAD geometry, passes at volumetric IoU >60% increase from 2/18 to 8/18. This is a targeted check, not a fresh full-dataset coverage claim. C52717 and C14347 lose their old passing scores after selecting the correct family: TSSOP body/lead defaults still need work. Four entries retain their previous selection where metadata conflicts or the alternative still scores better.

Example recovered string:

```
tssop20_p0.65mm_w3.9999mm_pw0.364mm_pl1.742mm_rounded0.182mm_pin1location(leftside,bottom)
```

body:
In the TPS61288 conversion, the real Altium 365 Viewer placed U1/U2's VOUT pin number `5` near the outer end of the pin. The export relied on Altium's default designator margin of 9 schematic units, which left too much space between the component body and the number.

Set an explicit native pin-number margin of **3 schematic units** (`0.15 circuit units × 20`) and enable custom positioning alongside the existing custom font. Numbers now sit near the component body in all four orientations. Pin-name positioning, font sizes, colors, pin geometry and connectivity are preserved.

Circuit JSON renders ordinary pin numbers at 0.15 circuit units, equivalent to 3 units at the converter's 20× scale. The converter used 0.2, producing a 4-unit font in the local Altium preview. Export native pin numbers as **Arial 3 pt** so their local preview size matches that scale.

The **3-unit body-side margin** from #162 is preserved. Pin-name font overrides, pin lengths, colors and connectivity are unchanged. The 35 updated SVG snapshots differ only in native pin-number font sizes; Circuit JSON panels are unchanged.

title: Match native pin marker sizes and fill to Circuit JSON
description: Adjusts Altium pin markers to match sizes and fill styles defined in Circuit JSON, ensuring proper visual representation and electrical behavior in exported schematics.
body:
Stacked on #163.

Altium's automatic pin markers are larger than Circuit JSON's markers and draw a line through the triangles. This exports white-filled native circles and triangles with the hairline stroke preset. Circle radius is **1.2 Altium units** (`0.06 × 20`); triangle side length is **2 units** (`0.1 × 20`), with depth √3 and half-width 1. Wires stop at the outer edge, leaving the interiors clear.

Pin names stay 2 units inside the body and numbers stay 3 units outside. This uses the native name-margin correction in [altiumts `07ecff9`](https://github.com/tscircuit/altiumts/commit/07ecff96b4a2421ed7ff05285cbf405279340a64), pinned by full Git hash. That upstream fix is currently on `codex/native-pin-name-margins` and has not been merged into altiumts main.

**Electrical behavior:** custom direction graphics replace inferred Input/Output/Bidirectional electrical types. Native pins use Passive, retaining connectivity while removing direction-based ERC checks inferred from those visual flags.

### Native Altium review files

- [Download the pin-marker comparison .SchDoc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-altium/7193b59feca8fc3c915d7044caa70ef0725d5dde/tests/assets/pin-marker-bubbles-1p2.SchDoc)
- [Download the automotive communication/VCC sheet .SchDoc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-altium/7193b59feca8fc3c915d7044caa70ef0725d5dde/tests/assets/automotive-mirror-communication-pin-markers.SchDoc)

These files were verified in real Altium Viewer. Links below point to this exact converter commit, so they show the same outputs as the files above.

### Pin-marker detail

Cropped from the Altium panel of the snapshot below; the drawing is unchanged.

![Enlarged Altium pin markers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-altium/7193b59feca8fc3c915d7044caa70ef0725d5dde/tests/assets/pin-markers-detail.svg)

[Open the enlarged marker snapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-altium/7193b59feca8fc3c915d7044caa70ef0725d5dde/tests/assets/pin-markers-detail.svg)

title: Fix native pin connection points at Circuit JSON terminals
description: Fixes the placement of native electrical terminals at the converted Circuit JSON schematic port center, ensuring accurate pin connection points in Altium.
body:
Stacked on #164.

The automotive CAN interface showed native pin connection dots next to U6's body and L7's symbol artwork. The thin-stem conversion placed zero-length electrical pins there and extended them with sheet wires, so Altium highlighted the wrong end of the visible pin.

This places every native electrical terminal at the converted Circuit JSON `schematic_port.center`. The exposed stem is component-owned artwork with `LINEWIDTH=0`; it ends outside filled markers. Pin-name and number margins compensate for the terminal move, preserving text positions, fonts and colors. The same path covers boxed chips, built-in symbols and custom symbols without checking `ftype`.

Validation covers all Circuit JSON component types in four orientations and all 226 pins across the automotive project's seven sheets. It also checks unchanged source-trace endpoints, no-connect markers, hairline strokes, marker fills and text placement. The Altiumts dependency is unchanged from #164.


### Review files

- [Automotive CAN interface — U6, L7 and passives](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-altium/75fc7419a44ef2cf36e87241ed53f134a63f818a/tests/assets/automotive-mirror-communication-pin-terminals.SchDoc)
- [Four pin orientations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-altium/75fc7419a44ef2cf36e87241ed53f134a63f818a/tests/assets/pin-connection-points.SchDoc)

In Altium Viewer, inspect the terminal where the pin meets the external trace. The pin marker should be at this outer endpoint, while its name and number remain near the body. These new files have been checked by parsing their native records and rendering their SVGs; interactive Altium Viewer verification is still pending.

title: Hide unsupported RISC-V category from TI navigation
description: Removes the unsupported RISC-V family mapping from the navigation filter, ensuring that no unsupported RISC-V tiles are displayed to users.
body:
The RISC-V tile was shown because its route reused TI's general MCU families, even though no verified RISC-V parts exist in the imported catalog. A read-only audit of all 67,549 stored records found no RISC-V, RISC V, or RISCV metadata references. Descriptions saying RISC alone describe other architectures and must not be classified as RISC-V.

Remove the unsupported family mapping so the existing navigation filter hides the tile. Preserve the route, query parameters, and empty JSON response for compatibility. Add a homepage regression; the existing route-contract test verifies the endpoint remains available.

Validation: full test suite, TypeScript, formatting, and diff checks passed. No D1 writes, TI API requests, or production deployment.

title: Fill DAC channel counts from explicit TI descriptions
description: Fills DAC channel counts from explicit TI descriptions to improve channel coverage in the DAC catalog.
body:
Most DAC channel cells remained blank after the parametric alias fix: only 33 of 1,361 stored DACs currently have detailed specifications. Many of the other records already have an explicit channel count in their TI Product Information description.

Use explicit descriptions such as `1-channel`, `quad-channel`, `1-ch`, and `stereo DAC` as a fallback when hydrating stored DAC rows. Structured TI specifications and existing explicit counts take precedence. Restrict extraction to DAC families and reject mixed ADC/DAC or conflicting counts; do not infer counts from model numbers, bit depth, or supply counts.

On the current live DAC snapshot, channel coverage increases from 33 to 799 rows without TI API requests or D1 writes. The remaining 562 rows still require specifications. Both displayed category values and channel filters use the hydrated count.

Validation: all 121 tests passed, including real TI description examples, precedence/ambiguity cases, and D1-backed category/filter coverage. TypeScript, formatting, diff checks, and Wrangler dry-run build passed. No production deployment performed.

title: Fix Linux processor results and missing TI specification columns
description: Fixes the Linux-capable Processors page by correctly querying TI processor families and mapping DACADC channel specifications, improving data accuracy and availability.
body:
The Linux-capable Processors page was empty because it queried `Arm-based processors`, while TI stores the relevant parts under leaf families such as `Multimedia & industrial networking SoCs`. DAC channel counts were also empty because the mapper did not recognize `Number of DAC channels`.

This change:
- Uses actual TI processor families while retaining per-part Linux/ARM/NPU classification. Preserves explicit CPU metadata and supports additional application processors when TI explicitly declares Linux support and a recognized core.
- Maps DAC/ADC channel aliases, settling time, INL, sample/update rates, regulator dropout/current/noise/PSRR, converter switching frequency/output count, and MCU interfaces/features with unit conversion. Ambiguous package-dependent values and unavailable specifications remain unknown.
- Interleaves missing specifications with remaining basic-information lookups (four specification turns per information turn), prioritizing stocked parts in mapped categories. Keeps the existing 1,500-request daily budget, gateway cooldowns, and update-only catalog behavior.
- Adds D1 indexes for the priority queues and per-family specification coverage in `/api/enrichment/status`.

Read-only production audit: the corrected classifier includes 228 stored Linux-capable processors (185 in stock), and the DAC alias recovers 33 existing channel counts. The broader missing-column issue also reflects incomplete enrichment: 1,652 of 67,549 parts had detailed specifications at audit time; all 1,022 precision DACs and 161 audio DACs were still pending. Those values will fill as the background job fetches TI specifications after its existing budget resets. This PR does not invent values to fill cells or insert new parts.

Validation: all 107 tests passed, including D1-backed category/filter regressions using sampled TI metadata and a scheduling/budget regression. TypeScript, formatting, diff checks, and Wrangler dry-run build passed. Migration 0006 was exercised in the test databases.

Deployment: apply migration 0006 and deploy the Worker (the existing `bun run deploy` command does both). Existing job state and its current quota reset are preserved. Production was not modified during this work.

title: Fix analog switch classification using TI configuration
description: Fixes incorrect classification of analog switches by using TIs configuration metadata to accurately filter and categorize switches and multiplexers.
body:
The Analog Switches page admitted any part in TI's combined switches/muxes family with at most two channels. TI counts independent banks as channels, so 4:1, 8:1, and 16:1 multiplexers such as CD4052, CD4051, and CD4067 incorrectly appeared alongside simple switches. The same rule excluded quad SPST switches.

Classify switches using TI's Configuration metadata instead: accept simple 1:1/2:1/1:2 paths and SPST/SPDT/DPST/DPDT configurations, and reject larger mux/crosspoint ratios. When configuration is absent, require an explicit analog/bilateral switch description without mux wording. Channel count remains available as a user filter.

The shared filter fixes both JSON and HTML results. Existing Analog Muxes results and endpoint contracts are preserved. This reads existing D1 metadata; no catalog re-import, migration, or additional TI requests are needed. The change takes effect when the updated Worker is deployed.

Validation:
- All 101 tests passed, including configuration cases and D1-backed JSON/HTML regressions for the reported parts, quad SPST inclusion, and continued mux availability.
- TypeScript, formatting, and git diff checks passed.
- Wrangler dry-run build passed; no production deployment performed.

title: Hide LCSC column and unsupported categories from TI search pages
description: Removes the empty LCSC column from HTML tables and hides categories without TI family mappings from the homepage and HTML category directory, while retaining existing category routes and JSON schemas.
body:
Remove the empty LCSC column from HTML tables and hide categories without TI family mappings from the homepage and HTML category directory. Mechanical switches, barrel jacks, connectors, and other unsupported categories are omitted; supported semiconductor categories such as analog switches remain. Existing category routes and JSON schemas remain available.

Validation: all 90 tests, typecheck, formatting, and dry-run build pass. The homepage regression check verifies supported tile order and the absence of switches/barrel jacks.
